title: Keep work and resume on producer deadline; record as timed out
summary: When a producer stage hits its deadline, keep the job's worktree edits and write a progress note. Record the job as timed out rather than failed, and have `athena retry` resume from the kept work with the note. Status output tells timed out from failed. The user narrowed this to the producer stage only: no verifier-stage timeouts and no multi-part planning. The audience is the Athena operator, who loses 20–30 minutes of work per timeout.

defaults_applied.how: Criteria check that edits are kept and the retry resumes from them, not that types exist.
cargo test, clippy and fmt --check must pass.
Producer stage only, per the user's narrowing.
Tests exercise the deadline and retry flow with the fake agent.
Keep the work at the point where the timeout discards it, rather than adding a workaround.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Scope is the producer stage only, per the user's reply. Verifier-stage timeouts and multi-part planning are excluded.
A deadline kill is currently recorded as killed or failed and the worktree is discarded; I did not confirm this by reading the code.
The progress note is a file in the job directory or worktree, passed into the retry producer's prompt.
Deliverable paths are guesses from a grep for 'deadline' and 'Killed'; I did not read the files.

acceptance_criteria.text: A test with the fake agent hits a producer deadline after editing files. Afterwards the edits remain in the job worktree, a progress note exists, and the job is recorded as timed out, not failed. Run: cargo test.
A test retries a timed-out job. The new producer starts from the kept worktree (not a clean checkout) and is given the progress note. Run: cargo test.
Status output distinguishes a timed-out job from a failed one, and the deadline reason (e.g. 'deadline of 1800s reached') is kept in the record. Run: cargo test.
A test shows existing records with killed or failed outcomes still deserialize unchanged. Run: cargo test.
The new timed-out outcome is documented and CHANGELOG.md mentions the change.
cargo test, cargo clippy and cargo fmt --check all pass with no new warnings.

out_of_scope: Splitting multi-part requests into one plan item per part
departures: Cost and time are above the reference because the change spans the agent, data and CLI crates and needs new retry-resume tests.
urgent_reason: Timeouts discard 20–30 minutes of producer work and force redo-work retries; keeping that work cuts wasted time.
